issues.description: Element(s): class name and field type for the saloon's stock. The problem statement (UML and text) declares a class named 'Stock' with methods add(String), take(String), findStockIngredient(String), addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient), and emptyStock(), and it shows SealSaloon having an association/attribute to Stock (SealSaloon.stock). The template repository provides a fully implemented class named 'Inventory' (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Inventory.java) that implements the expected methods, and Stock.java in the template is empty. The solution repository's SealSaloon uses a static Inventory field (private static final Inventory stock = new Inventory()). This name/type mismatch (Stock vs Inventory) leaves students unsure which class they must implement/use, and can cause compilation or design confusion if they follow the UML (expecting Stock) but the template/solution use Inventory.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the class name consistent across all artifacts. Preferred option: rename Inventory (file and class) to Stock (update src/de/tum/cit/ase/Inventory.java -> src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java and change 'class Inventory' to 'class Stock'), and update all references (SealSaloon and any imports) so the UML, problem text, template, and solution consistently refer to Stock. Alternate acceptable fixes: (A) Update the problem statement and UML to refer to 'Inventory' instead of 'Stock', or (B) provide a concrete Stock.java wrapper that delegates to Inventory (keeping Inventory but adding a Stock class that forwards the required methods) and update the template so SealSaloon.stock is typed as Stock. Ensure one canonical name is used everywhere so students know which class to implement and use.

issues.description: Concept: the saloon's ingredient storage. Problem statement (UML and text) refers to a class named 'Stock' and describes a SealSaloon.stock attribute of type Stock. The provided template and the reference solution instead provide a class named 'Inventory' (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Inventory.java) which implements the methods and behaviour described for Stock (add, take, findStockIngredient, addToStockIngredients, emptyStock). Additionally, there is an empty file src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java in the template/solution repositories. This naming mismatch (Stock vs Inventory) means students reading the problem will look for a Stock class and methods named as in the UML, but the concrete implementation in the template is named Inventory; the empty Stock.java may further mislead students into thinking Stock is intentional or is where they must implement functionality. This discrepancy prevents a clear mapping from problem requirements to the provided code and increases cognitive load.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the identifier for the stock concept across all artifacts. Option A (recommended): rename the Inventory class and its file to Stock (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java), remove the empty Stock.java stub, and update any references (SealSaloon.stock, imports) so the class name matches the UML and prose. Option B: alternatively, update the problem statement and UML to use 'Inventory' instead of 'Stock' so they match the template/solution. Ensure SealSaloon and all example code consistently use the same class name and that the file contents are non-empty and implement the described methods (add, take, findStockIngredient, addToStockIngredients, emptyStock).
